answer: We define a Sybil-resistant game where each identity requires a dynamic opportunity-cost bond. Within a comet consensus engine, staking collateral must exceed the expected yield delta to enforce subgame-perfect equilibrium. When an adversary attempts identity multiplication, a zero-knowledge verifiable delay function acts as a protective reef that escalates computation costs. Consequently, the slashing penalty renders the expected utility of the attack strictly negative, guaranteeing a robust Nash equilibrium.
